newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais say Burma ready to take back Karen refugees.
newsitem.headline: Thais say Burma ready to take back Karen refugees.

text.p: Thailand's army chief said on Tuesday that the Burmese military had agreed to take back Karen refugees sheltering on the Thai side of the border, but only if they wanted to go.

Burmese troops have attacked and overrun mobile camps of the the rebel Karen National Union (KNU) in recent weeks, prompting tens of thousands of Karens to flee to Thailand, swelling the number of Karen refugees already in the country.

Only those returning willingly to Burma would be accepted, Thai army commander in chief General Chetta Thanajaro said after meeting his Burmese counterpart, General Maung Aye, at the Burma border town of Tachilek.
"The meeting was very successful, especially when they (Burmese) agreed to take the refugees back," Chetta told reporters after the three hours of talks.
"The Burmese side said they are willing to take back only those who...return on a voluntary basis."
Burmese officials were not available for comment.
More than 70,000 ethnic Karens with Burmese nationality, family members and followers of the KNU have fled fighting in Burma have lived in sprawling camps inside Thailand since the 1980s.
The KNU, formed in 1948 to seek greater autonomy for eastern Karen state, has rejected several peace overtures from Rangoon and refused to lay down arms.
Burma in the past has repeatedly charged that KNU rebels have been hiding in the Thai refugee camps. Rangoon has also refused to take back the refugees citing lack of documentation.
The Thai army said last week that it would strictly screen KNU rebels out from civilians and centralise the camps.

A KNU source told Reuters on Tuesday that several KNU officials who fled fighting last week between the KNU and Burmese troops into the western Thai town of Umphang had been rounded up over the weekend and housed in a central location.
Maung Aye, also vice chairman of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), on Tuesday was quoted as saying Burma would continue its peace efforts with the rebels.

"...The government always welcomes the KNU although they neglect peace and the armed forces and the entire people warmly welcome U Saw Tha Mu He and members for their efforts for peace," Maung Aye was quoted as saying by official media.
He was speaking at a welcoming ceremony for 496 KNU rebels, including Saw Tha Mui He, commander of the KNU's 16 battalion, who surrendered to the government in Karen state on Monday, the media said.
